positive: Initialize constants from each permitted source and initialize specparams from other specparams.

edge: Use signing and packed dimensions as an implicit parameter type.
negative: Use a nonconstant parameter initializer.
positive: Declare typed and implicit value parameters/localparams with dimensions and multiple assignments.

edge: Declare multiple instances with differing variable dimensions in one declaration.
negative: Use a class-new initializer on an ordinary nonclass declarator.
positive: Declare ordinary, dynamic-array, and class variables using their respective optional initializers.

edge: Release a force while a procedural assign remains active and observe that source regain control.
positive: Apply normal assignment, procedural assign, and force in sequence and observe the stated precedence.

edge: Use dynamic versus constant indices to exercise longest-static-prefix expansion.
negative: Continuously and procedurally write terms sharing the same longest static prefix.
Apply two continuous assignments to the same array element.
positive: Continuously drive one structure member and procedurally write a different member.
Use separate continuous assignments for distinct packed bits.

edge: Contrast identical declaration-assignment syntax on a wire and on a logic variable.
negative: Combine declaration initialization with a continuous assignment where both target the same longest static prefix.
positive: Initialize a variable in its declaration and subsequently procedurally assign it.

edge: Change the variable multiple times and verify each value reaches the connected net.
positive: Connect an output variable through a port to a net and observe updates propagate continuously.

edge: Write the same variable from sequential statements in one time slot with deterministic execution order.
positive: Perform ordered procedural writes to a variable and observe the final write's value.

edge: Contrast variable retention with an ordinary net following its current drivers.
positive: Assign a variable, advance simulation without another write, and observe retention.

edge: Contrast separate independently driven elements with overlapping writes to one element.
negative: Drive the same variable from two continuous assignments.
positive: Drive a variable from one continuous assignment.

edge: Exercise small-width underflow.
positive: Increment an all-ones vector and observe wrap to zero.

edge: Connect through a signed port.
positive: Compare unqualified and signed logic vectors.
Declare ascending, descending, negative-bound, and equal-bound ranges.

edge: Use negative range bounds.
positive: Verify addressing and significance on descending and ascending vectors.

edge: Use zero and negative bounds.
negative: Use variable or x/z-containing bounds.
positive: Use parameter-derived integer bounds.

edge: Use packed and unpacked dimensions together and verify the packed dimension satisfies the condition.
negative: Apply vectored or scalared to a scalar net without a packed dimension.
positive: Declare a packed wire vector as vectored or scalared.

edge: Contrast member-type access with object construction and with a nonvirtual equivalent class.
negative: Attempt to construct an object of the virtual typedef-container class.
positive: Declare a virtual parameterized class with typedef members and use specialized member types.

edge: Contrast the null default with a virtual-interface handle after assigning an interface instance.
positive: Compare an uninitialized virtual-interface handle with null.

edge: Contrast void function and task invocation contexts.
negative: Use a void function call where a value expression is required.
positive: Declare and call a void function for its side effects.

edge: Switch between a void tag and a payload-bearing tag.
positive: Declare and construct a tagged union with a void member.

edge: Use multiple four-state drivers on each synonym.
positive: Apply corresponding declarations and drivers to wand and triand and observe identical results.

edge: Check z/z, x/z, and 0/1 as distinct resolution boundaries.
positive: Exercise all unordered pairs of 0, 1, x, and z on two equal-strength wire drivers.

edge: Use multiple drivers on both wire and tri to demonstrate that the naming suggestion is not a legality distinction.
positive: Apply identical declarations and drivers to corresponding wire and tri nets and observe equal behavior.

edge: Distinguish 0/x, 1/x, 1/z, and z/z outcomes.
positive: Exercise every unordered pair of 0, 1, x, and z on equal-strength wand drivers.

edge: Distinguish 1/x, 0/x, 0/z, and z/z outcomes.
positive: Exercise every unordered pair of 0, 1, x, and z on equal-strength wor drivers.

edge: Use multiple four-state drivers on each synonym.
positive: Apply corresponding declarations and drivers to wor and trior and observe identical results.

edge: Use explicitly one-bit operands to isolate complement behavior from reduction or truth conversion.
positive: Apply logical negation to 1'b0 and 1'b1 and observe 1 and 0 respectively.

edge: Use a run-time multiplier evaluating to zero.
positive: Replicate a nonempty string expression zero times and verify string type, empty value, and zero length.
